aiOverview.content: United States Treasury securities are safe, low-risk government debt instruments issued by the U.S. Department of the Treasury to finance government spending. They are backed by the full faith and credit of the U.S. government, providing fixed interest payments or discounted purchasing options. Key types include Treasury Bills (short-term), Notes (medium-term), and Bonds (long-term), which can be purchased through TreasuryDirect.Types of U.S. Treasury SecuritiesTreasury Bills (T-Bills): Short-term securities maturing in 4, 8, 13, 26, or 52 weeks, sold at a discount.Treasury Notes (T-Notes): Fixed-principal securities with maturities of 2, 3, 5, 7, or 10 years, paying interest every six months.Treasury Bonds: Long-term, 20 or 30-year maturities, paying interest every six months.Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities (TIPS): Marketable securities designed to protect against inflation; the principal increases with inflation.Savings Bonds: Non-marketable securities (Series I or Series EE) that cannot be sold on the secondary market.Key Features & BenefitsHigh Safety: Backed by the U.S. government, they are considered to have almost no default risk.Marketability: Most Treasuries (Bills, Notes, Bonds, TIPS) can be bought and sold in the secondary market.Tax Benefits: Interest is exempt from state and local income taxes, but subject to federal tax.Purchasing: Individuals can buy directly from the government through the TreasuryDirect website.Note: Treasury securities typically offer lower yields compared to higher-risk investments due to their safety.
